ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reservoir Sampling for Time-Varying Offsets
PROPOSAL: Implement a variant of reservoir sampling to tackle the unknown, time-dependent additive offsets. At each time step in training, store the state transition and observation tuples in a reservoir buffer, with a probability inversely proportional to the buffer's current size. This will over-sample states and observations from the beginning of an episode, creating an unbiased distribution reflecting the offsets present at the time of sampling. When training a policy, use this buffer to learn from the shifted observations and states, effectively training on data seen during offset intervals. Additionally, to allow for varying offset sizes, add an offset magnitude component to the state transition and observation tuples.
CONTROLS: Standard offline RL methods (e.g. BCQ, TD3, SAC), vanilla reservoir sampling
COST: 5 GPU-hours (RL + reservoir sampling implementation)
PREDICTION: We expect improved offline RL performance under time-varying offsets when compared to standard offline RL methods, but the improvement may not generalize across different domain settings and types of offsets, and reservoir sampling's bias reduction might be imperfect for extremely sparse or bursty offset patterns.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Unsupervised Discovery of Time-Series Patterns in Offsets
PROPOSAL: Employ a robust, unsupervised time-series analysis technique to identify persistent patterns in the offsets of training episodes. This will help identify the underlying temporal structure of the offsets, enabling the model to adapt to different types of offsets more effectively. Train a model such as Prophet or a combination of seasonal decomposition and time-series regression (e.g. STL decomposition) to capture periodic, trend, and anomaly features in the offsets. Then, integrate this model's predictions into the state transition and observation tuples used for offline RL training, compensating for the discovered patterns in the offsets.
CONTROLS: Standard offline RL methods (without any time-series pattern compensation), reservoir sampling (Turn 1's proposal)
COST: 7 GPU-hours (unsupervised time-series analysis + offline RL training)
PREDICTION: Robust offline RL performance should be expected across various offset patterns and types, as the model adapts to the structure within the offsets. However, improved performance is expected only when the discovered patterns are consistent and indicative of the offset intervals used during training, and if the time-series model can effectively capture anomalies and uncertainty in the offset patterns.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cross-Episode Offset Causal Alignment
PROPOSAL: Propose a novel concept: cross-episode offset causal alignment. Given the history of past offsets (if available) or the nature of the discovered patterns in offsets, create a week alignment model that represents how the offsets from previous episodes relate to their future counterparts. This model would track inter-episode correlations and dependencies, producing an embedding of off-by offsets that accounts for the likely shifts between episodes. Integrate this embedding as an auxiliary loss into the offline RL objective, encouraging the policy to consider an unseen episode's offset evolution when predicting its future behavior.
CONTROLS: Reservoir sampling + time-series analysis (Turns 1 and 2), vanilla offline RL methods
COST: 10 GPU-hours (week alignment model + offline RL training with auxiliary loss)
PREDICTION: The addition of cross-episode offset causal alignment should help improve offline RL performance for future episodes with unseen offset patterns, enabling more informed predictions under unknown offsets. However, performance might be negatively affected for episodes with strongly anti-correlated offsets or if the week alignment model struggles to capture underlying offset structures, especially in the early stages of training when it has limited history of offsets to draw from.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: REVISED Cross-Episode Offset Causal Alignment
PROPOSAL: Revise the cross-episode offset causal alignment proposal by dropping the history of past offsets and instead using the time-series analysis model (Turn 2) to infer inter-episode dependencies. This model already captures patterns in the offsets, which can be leveraged to estimate their probable values in unseen episodes. Modify the policy to use these estimated offset predictions rather than the auxiliary loss, producing a policy that more directly responds to likely future offset values. This approach also reduces model complexity and allows for more straightforward offline RL training with the inferred time-series patterns.
CONTROLS: Reservoir sampling + time-series analysis, vanilla offline RL methods
COST: 5 GPU-hours (policy modification + offline RL training)
PREDICTION: The revised proposal should retain the advantages of the original idea (i.e., better predictions for future episodes) while reducing the model's overall complexity and improving training efficiency. Moreover, since this approach focuses on capturing existing patterns in the offsets, its performance might be less hampered by anti-correlated offsets and unknown offset structures compared to the original proposal.

ACTION: REVISE 4
TITLE: REVISED Partial Observability-Aware Goal Sampling
PROPOSAL: Revise the partial observability-aware goal sampling proposal to focus on the estimation of state-action pairs that are likely to be corresponding under observation shifts, such as those captured by the REVISED Cross-Episode Offset Causal Alignment model (Turn 5). Use the state- offset predictions from that model to augment the reservoir sampling buffer with potentially corresponding state-action pairs under time-varying offsets. This enhancement should help the policy generalize to unseen offset patterns more effectively and reduce the impact of observation noise or missing information on goal-oriented learning.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Robust Optimization for Offset-Aware Offline RL
PROPOSAL: Introduce a robust optimization framework to account for the uncertainty and noise present in the offset-aware offline RL problem. Specifically, we propose using a distributionally robust optimization (DRO) approach that seeks to optimize the policy with respect to the worst-case offset distribution within a given ambiguity set. This enables the policy to be more robust to unseen offset patterns and mitigates the negative impact of noisy or missing observations. To construct the ambiguity set, use the REVISED Cross-Episode Offset Causal Alignment model (Turn 5) to estimate the offset distribution and incorporate additional uncertainty terms to capture any remaining ambiguity.
CONTROLS: Standard offline RL methods, reservoir sampling, REVISED Cross-Episode Offset Causal Alignment, REVISED Partial Observability-Aware Goal Sampling
COST: 8 GPU-hours (DRO framework + offline RL training with ambiguity set)
PREDICTION: Incorporating robust optimization should significantly enhance the stability and adaptability of the offline RL policy under unknown time-varying offsets, making it more resilient to real-world complexities such as missing or noisy observations. However, the added complexity of the DRO framework may come with increased computational costs and may be challenging to optimize for in practice.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transferable Offset Abstraction
PROPOSAL: Introduce a novel abstraction mechanism to enable offset-aware offline RL policies to transfer knowledge across episodes with different, but related, time-varying offsets. Specifically, use a graph neural network architecture to learn a representation of the offset space, where nodes correspond to different offset values and edges capture the relationships between them. Represent the policy as a subset of this graph and prune isolated nodes and edges to encourage the policy to focus on the most relevant offset relationships. During training, use the REVISED Partial Observability-Aware Goal Sampling (Turn 7) to refine the policy, while testing involves applying the transferable offset abstraction to unseen episodes.
CONTROLS: Standard offline RL methods, reservoir sampling, REVISED Cross-Episode Offset Causal Alignment, REVISED Partial Observability-Aware Goal Sampling, Robust Optimization for Offset-Aware Offline RL
COST: 15 GPU-hours (graph neural network + offline RL training and testing)
PREDICTION: The use of transferable offset abstraction should enable the offline RL policy to generalize better across episodes with varying time-varying offsets, allowing for improved performance under real-world complexities. However, the added complexity of the graph neural network may require careful tuning of hyperparameters and the abstraction mechanism may not always capture the most relevant relationships between offset values.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Agent Evaluation and Fine-Tuning for Real-World Environments
PROPOSAL: Leverage multi-agent evaluations and fine-tuning to augment the offline RL policies in the real-world domains of robot navigation and manipulation. Create a set of diverse, experienced agents to interact with the target domain, and use these agents to generate additional labeled data, which can be used to fine-tune the policies. Incorporate this fine-tuned policy into the transferable offset abstraction framework, enabling further refinement and adaptation to real-world complexities. This setup should improve the policy's robustness and adaptability in real-world environments with time-varying offsets.
CONTROLS: Standard offline RL methods, reservoir sampling, REVISED Cross-Episode Offset Causal Alignment, REVISED Partial Observability-Aware Goal Sampling, Robust Optimization for Offset-Aware Offline RL, Transferable Offset Abstraction
COST: 20 GPU-hours (multi-agent evaluation and fine-tuning + offline RL training and testing)
PREDICTION: The incorporation of multi-agent evaluations and fine-tuning should enable significant improvements in the policy's robustness and adaptability in real-world environments. This is because the multi-agent setup allows for a more diverse and extensive exploration of the domain, which should generalize better to unseen scenarios with time-varying offsets.

PROPOSAL: The OGE algorithm forecasts the evolution of the observation function by first computing the differences between cleaning, stationary trajectory segments of the offline RL dataset and a ground-truth version of the same segments. The differences are used to construct an auxiliary objective minimizing the accumulation of deflection between predicted and observed trajectories at each turn during the organic episodes of training on the dataset. Thus, OGE learns to implicitly anticipate each novel offset by preparing itself progressively at each transition over existing data sequences, leveraging subtleties hidden in behavior otherwise obscured.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Image-Based Shift Localization (IBSL)
PROPOSAL: IBSL is a modular, model-agnostic method for identifying shifts in individual dimensions of the agent's observation function. IBSL trains an image transformer to predict the difference between the clean observation and its shifted version. The predicted differences are then used to estimate the degree of shift in each dimension. This approach is modular and can be used to complement existing offline RL algorithms, helping them detect and adapt to shifts without modifying their core architecture.
CONTROLS: Same offline dataset used in OGE, baseline without shift detection, baseline with data drift compensation
COST: 500
PREDICTION: IBSL should outperform baseline methods in identifying shifts, and in combination with OGE, the ensemble should improve policy generalization; the separate detection of shifts may however fail when those shifts affect multiple dimensions, or when the offsets are too complex, leading to incompatible predictions.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Observational Gap Exploration (OGE) Algorithm with Hierarchical Offsets Estimation
PROPOSAL: To improve robustness, the revised OGE algorithm will first identify the presence of shifts using IBSL (dimension-wise, as in IBSL) and then learn to model hierarchical temporal relationships between the offsets. The algorithm will decompose the offsets into coarse-grained (episode-level) and fine-grained (step-level) shifts, allowing for more nuanced modeling of the observation function's evolution.
CONTROLS: Same as before, baseline without OGE and without IBSL, baseline with OGE without hierarchical modeling, baseline with IBSL without hierarchical modeling
COST: 2000 (adds to the original 1000, totaling 3000)
PREDICTION: Hierarchical offsets estimation should improve policy generalization by better capturing the relationship between offsets over time and reducing overfitting; the increased computational cost may be justified by improved results in harder cases; however, the additive offset amplitudes may still pose challenges when wrongly modeled or estimated, causing policy novelty to grow explosively.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Investigating Temporal State Estimation for Non-Stationary Observation Functions in Offline RL
PROPOSAL: Evaluate an offline RL baseline (e.g., Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG)) on a synthetic dataset with episodically evolving observation functions. Introduce temporal state estimation within the offline RL framework by incorporating a convolutional neural network (CNN) to predict per-episode offsets from past observations and actions. This is a basic experiment to understand the feasibility of state estimation for non-stationary observation functions.
CONTROLS: 
1. A standard offline RL baseline without temporal state estimation.
2. A modified version of the baseline using static state estimation (e.g., a Gaussian mixture model to infer the per-dimension offsets).
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The baseline with temporal state estimation will outperform the static state estimation variant in terms of average episode return. The baseline without temporal state estimation will perform poorly due to its inability to allocate for state misalignment.

Expected results: a clear gap between the three variants, validating the importance of temporal state estimation in addressing non-stationarity in offline RL.

Turn 1 Result: the initial assessment is favorable for temporal state estimation with offline RL.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Hierarchical Temporal Offset Prediction for Offline RL
PROPOSAL: Revise proposal 1 by incorporating a hierarchical structure in the temporal state estimation component. The architecture will consist of a lightweight predictor (a single fully connected layer or a small recurrent network) to estimate the per-episode offset from the past few observations and actions, and a more complex model (e.g., a neural network with multiple layers or a long short-term memory (LSTM) network) that can leverage the output of the lightweight predictor and the past offset history (possibly obtained through a buffer) to make more accurate predictions for longer horizons. This hierarchical structure will be evaluated on the same synthetic dataset as proposal 1, with the same controls.
CONTROLS: 
1. The baseline without temporal state estimation.
2. The static state estimation variant discussed in proposal 1.
3. The revised temporal state estimation variant with a single predictor (i.e., no hierarchical structure).
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The hierarchical temporal state estimation variant will outperform the single predictor variant, both in terms of accuracy and robustness against unseen offset patterns. The baseline will be outperformed by both variants.

Expected results: an improvement in the state estimation performance when using a hierarchical structure, validating the benefits of hierarchical modeling for learning non-stationarity in offline RL.

Turn 2 Result: building upon the first proposal by incorporating a hierarchical structure.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Hierarchical Temporal Offset Prediction for Offline RL
PROPOSAL: Enhance proposal 2 by incorporating an epoch-based offset forgetting mechanism. This will allow the model to focus on the most recent offsets and gradually forget the offset values from previous episodes, mitigating the impact of long-term offset history that may become outdated. The epoch-based offset forgetting mechanism will be implemented by introducing an additional buffer with a limited capacity to store the most recent offset values, which will be used as input for the hierarchical offset predictor. The introduction of this mechanism will allow the model to adapt to changing offset patterns in a more dynamic fashion.
CONTROLS: 
1. The baseline without temporal state estimation.
2. The static state estimation variant discussed in proposal 1.
3. The revised hierarchical temporal state estimation variant without the epoch-based offset forgetting mechanism.
4. A version of the revised hierarchical temporal state estimation variant with the epoch-based offset forgetting mechanism and an extended buffer capacity to store a greater amount of offset history.
COST: 250 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The revised hierarchical temporal state estimation variant with the epoch-based offset forgetting mechanism will outperform the baseline without temporal state estimation and the static state estimation variant, in terms of both accuracy and adaptability to changing offset patterns. The extended buffer capacity will lead to improved performance in the presence of very long-term offset shifts, but may also increase the risk of overfitting to less generalizable patterns.

Turn 3 Result: an enhancement of the hierarchical temporal state estimation variant by incorporating an offset forgetting mechanism.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Uncertainty Estimates in Temporal State Estimation
PROPOSAL: Evaluate a variant of the hierarchical temporal offset prediction algorithm (revise 2) that incorporates uncertainty estimates in its offset predictions. This will be achieved by using Bayesian neural networks (BNNs) to represent the hierarchical offset predictor, which will output both point predictions and uncertainty estimates for the offset values. These uncertainty estimates will be used to compute a confidence-based loss function for the offset prediction task, allowing the model to focus on predictions with higher confidence and reduce the influence of predictions with high uncertainty. The BNN variant will be evaluated on the same synthetic dataset as previous proposals, with additional metrics to assess the model's uncertainty estimates and their relation to the true offset values.
CONTROLS: 
1. The baseline without temporal state estimation.
2. The static state estimation variant discussed in proposal 1.
3. The revised hierarchical temporal state estimation variant without uncertainty estimates (i.e., the version with the epoch-based offset forgetting mechanism).
4. The BNN variant with uncertainty estimates.
COST: 220 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The BNN variant will exhibit improved performance in terms of both accuracy and adaptability to changing offset patterns, as the confidence-based loss function will allow the model to reduce the impact of high-uncertainty predictions. Additionally, the BNN variant will provide valuable insights into the model's uncertainty estimates and their relation to the true offset values.

Expected results: an improved performance when incorporating uncertainty estimates in temporal state estimation for non-stationary observation functions in offline RL.

Turn 4 Result: an extension of the hierarchical temporal state estimation variant by incorporating uncertainty estimates using Bayesian neural networks.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Evaluating Temporal State Estimation in Offline RL on Synthetic Robot Navigation Data
PROPOSAL: Evaluate the performance of the hierarchical temporal offset prediction algorithm (revise 2) with uncertainty estimates (study 3) on a synthetic robot navigation dataset with episodically evolving observation functions. The dataset will be simulated using a popular robot simulator (e.g., Gazebo) and will include scenarios with diverse offset patterns, such as constant, linear, and non-linear offsets. The performance of the algorithm will be compared to the baseline without temporal state estimation and the static state estimation variant discussed in proposal 1. Additional metrics will be used to assess the model's ability to generalize to unseen offset patterns and to navigate the robot safely in scenarios with high uncertainty.
CONTROLS: 
1. The baseline without temporal state estimation.
2. The static state estimation variant discussed in proposal 1.
3. The revised hierarchical temporal state estimation variant without uncertainty estimates (i.e., the version with the epoch-based offset forgetting mechanism).
4. The BNN variant with uncertainty estimates.
5. A variant of the BNN algorithm that uses a more advanced robot navigation controller (e.g., a Model Predictive Control (MPC) controller) to navigate the robot in scenarios with high uncertainty.
COST: 320 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The BNN variant will exhibit improved performance in terms of both accuracy and generalization to unseen offset patterns on the robot navigation dataset. The algorithm will be able to navigate the robot safely in scenarios with high uncertainty, and the MPC controller will further improve the agent's ability to handle complex navigation tasks.

Expected results: an improved performance on a realistic synthetic robot navigation dataset, demonstrating the effectiveness of temporal state estimation for non-stationary observation functions in offline RL.

Turn 5 Result: evaluating the hierarchical temporal state estimation variant using a realistic synthetic robot navigation dataset.

ACTION: REVISE 4
TITLE: Evaluating Temporal State Estimation in Offline RL on Synthetic Robot Navigation Data
PROPOSAL: Introduce a new control group in the synthetic robot navigation dataset experiment (study 4) that represents a real-world scenario where the offset values are not perfectly captured by the hierarchical temporal offset prediction algorithm (revise 2) with uncertainty estimates (study 3). This will be achieved by introducing a "sparse" offset pattern where the offset values are only partially available, and the algorithm must adapt to this new scenario. The performance of the algorithm will be compared to the baseline without temporal state estimation and the static state estimation variant discussed in proposal 1, as well as the new control group with sparse offset patterns.
CONTROLS: 
1. The baseline without temporal state estimation.
2. The static state estimation variant discussed in proposal 1.
3. The revised hierarchical temporal state estimation variant without uncertainty estimates (i.e., the version with the epoch-based offset forgetting mechanism).
4. The BNN variant with uncertainty estimates.
5. A variant of the BNN algorithm that uses a more advanced robot navigation controller (e.g., a Model Predictive Control (MPC) controller) to navigate the robot in scenarios with high uncertainty.
6. A new control group with sparse offset patterns.
COST: 380 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The BNN variant will exhibit limited performance in the control group with sparse offset patterns, as the algorithm's ability to capture the complex offset dynamics will be impaired by the lack of data. The other control groups will still perform well, but the gap between the BNN variant and the baseline without temporal state estimation will be more pronounced.

Expected results: a realistic evaluation of the algorithm's performance in a scenario with sparse offset patterns, highlighting the need for further research in this area.

Turn 6 Result: an extension of the synthetic robot navigation dataset experiment to include a new control group with sparse offset patterns.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Investigating Transfer Learning for Offline RL in Robot Manipulation Tasks
PROPOSAL: Evaluate the performance of the hierarchical temporal offset prediction algorithm (revise 2) with uncertainty estimates (study 3) on a synthetic robot manipulation dataset with episodically evolving observation functions. The dataset will be simulated using a popular robot simulator (e.g., Gazebo) and will include scenarios with diverse offset patterns, such as constant, linear, and non-linear offsets. The performance of the algorithm will be compared to the baseline without temporal state estimation and the static state estimation variant discussed in proposal 1. Additionally, an experiment will be conducted to evaluate the transfer learning capabilities of the algorithm, where the model is trained on a different robot manipulation task and then fine-tuned on the new task with different offset patterns.
CONTROLS: 
1. The baseline without temporal state estimation.
2. The static state estimation variant discussed in proposal 1.
3. The revised hierarchical temporal state estimation variant without uncertainty estimates (i.e., the version with the epoch-based offset forgetting mechanism).
4. The BNN variant with uncertainty estimates.
5. A variant of the BNN algorithm that uses a more advanced robot navigation controller (e.g., a Model Predictive Control (MPC) controller) to navigate the robot in scenarios with high uncertainty.
6. A new control group with sparse offset patterns.
